# Played & Made — Life in Games (Played&Made)

> Interactive personal video game timeline builder, 4234-game historical lineage tree, game lore & deep-cuts trivia, and tribute to the human makers, studios, and hardware engineers behind video games.

Canonical URL: https://johanheurlin.github.io/inspired-by/
Author: Johan Heurlin

## Core Capabilities & Sections
- **Personal Gaming Timeline (#timeline & #picks)**: Build a year-by-year childhood or game-industry career timeline across 71 consoles, home computers, and regional platforms (including Amiga, Commodore 64, NES, Dendy, Subor, Sharp X68000, NEC PC-98, Vectrex, PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC), with shareable serverless links and PNG cards.
- **Video Game Family Tree (#explore)**: Trace 4234 games and 2802 primary-source inspiration links from 1950s lab mainframes and tabletop wargames to modern releases, documenting what each studio built on and what it added.
- **Game Lore & Lineage Trivia (#trivia)**: 6-mode interactive quiz covering Deep-Cut Gaming & Industry Lore, Lineage, Launch Year, Studio, Country, and System.
- **The Vault — Cancelled Games, Sunsetted Worlds & Hardware Folklore (#vault)**: Honors unshipped developer craft (Project Titan -> Overwatch, Van Buren -> Fallout: New Vegas, Star Wars 1313, Silent Hills, Thrill Kill -> Wu-Tang: Shaolin Style, Star Fox 2), sunsetted online worlds (Glitch -> Slack, Chromehounds, Star Wars Galaxies, City of Heroes, Echo VR, Knockout City), and strange-but-true gaming history (Gizmondo, Atari's Alamogordo New Mexico cartridge dig, TecToy Brazil, Sega Channel, Satellaview, Desert Bus).
- **Genres, Mechanics & Game Prices vs. Inflation (#mechanics, #genres, #boardgames, #prices)**: Explores 16 core mechanics, 30 genres, 14 tabletop roots, and 1977–2026 game prices in nominal vs. 2026 CPI-adjusted dollars compared against movies, concerts, food, and rent.
- **Makers, Studios & Global Map (#studios, #gratitude, #world)**: Profiles 75 studios (active and shuttered, tracing alumni diaspora), 35 pioneers, 26 hardware engineering teams, 46 countries, and downloadable Thank-You Postcards for game developers.
